Get the green ring and coins at your own risk. It's tough getting them without falling into the Munchers. Along your travels, you'll see two coins below. Glide down to them and enter the false wall with a brick containing a Invincibility Star that you'll need to run across the munchers and get Star Coin #3. Carefully run along the top of the stars to reach the exit.)

W4- Frosted Glacierv 2- Cooligan Fields / Cooligan Shrooms (55,56)

(The Cooligans come slipping in on the ice. Don't you wish you had the Penguin suit now so you can do the same? Unfortunately, you got to wait till you reach Star Road which you must have all Star Coins up to this point and beat the game. You must stomp on them twice to kill them. The first hit knocks off their glasses. Wait for an opportunity to get Star Coin #1 when it's clear. Avoid the flocks of Cooligans and you reach the checkpoint flag.

Get the red ring and coins and beware of Cooligans coming out of pipes. If you stay close to the wall, they'll sail over your head so you can get past them easier. Star Coin #2 is shortly after the slope. You will see a Cooligan sliding on its belly back and forth over the bricks. Knock them loose to get rid of the Cooligan and do a wall jump off the pipe to get the Star Coin. Eventually, you will see flocks of Cooligans and you can use them for leverage to get on the higher platforms to get Star Coin #3 then head for the exit.)

W4- Frosted Glacier 3- Prickly Goombas! / Fire and Ice (57,58)

(The Goombas have gotten tired of people stomping on them. Now some of them in this level have shielded themselves with thorn suit that can be burned away and make them vulnerable to other attacks. You don't really need Fire Mario. The VFTs are your friends here as they can burn the armor off themselves and so can the Fire Bros. Remember this bit of info when you need to get into the upside down pipe leading to Star Coin #1. You also meet Blue Yoshi who can blow bubbles that turn captured enemies into coins to collect. Hit the checkpoint flag after you get out.

Run along the ice wheel and into the hidden wall where a Yoshi hides in the ? block. Yoshi can stand on the thorn of the Prickly Goombas without getting hurt. This is important when you go for Star Coin #2 which is in the green pipe above the next rolling ice wheel. Enter the golden pipe to exit out. Once out, use Yoshi's hover jump to get Star Coin #3 and get past the ice wheels, Piranha Plants and Fire Bros. and go for the exit.)

W4- Frosted Glacier 4- Scaling the Mountainside / Weighty Waddlewings (59,60)

(Get through Koopa Troopas, Waddlewings, and Bullet Bills. There is a pit that looks like a secret spot but it is not. What you want to do is grab onto the wall in the pit and wall jump your way out as some bricks will appear and provide a "staircase" effect so you can jump up and get the Acorn in the ? block if you lack it then glide jump to the left to go in a secret spot with lots of coins and a 1-up. Go back to the right and use the left scale to raise the right one and then get on the right one and glide jump to get Star Coin #1. Star Coin #2 is shortly ahead to the right that you can't miss it. Continue right to get the checkpoint flag.

If you need a 1-up, stay low and there is a hidden 1-up at the top of that wall pocket. There are coins you can get by going around but it's not really worth any risks. There are two ways to reach Star Coin #3 which is hidden to the left of those two coins you may see. Get on top of the cliff on the right then glide to the left and get it or you can use the Bullet Bills for leverage. Get the red ring and manipulate the scales to get all the red rings. Get past the Banzai Bills and hit the exit pole.)

W4- Frosted Glacier 5- Icicle Caverns / Ice-Slide Expressway (61,62)

(Watch out for the giant icicle coming down on the way to the pipe and go down. You have Buzzy Beetles and icicles to deal with. When you get past the two platforms that rise and fall you'll see a giant icicle. Don't jump to the next cliff, run through the wall and get Star Coin #1. Gather the red ring and you'll need to be quick to get the red coins because those icicles are no joke. Get the checkpoint flag and move on. Trigger the next giant icicle. The icicles in this next section will not fall. Stomp on the Ice Bro for leverage to get inside the pipe above. Let the giant icicles fall so you can get Star Coin #2. The icicles will start to fall again but you can just run like the wind until the end. Go up the pipe on the far right if you were fast enough to make it there and you can get Star Coin #3 when you exit out and head for the exit.)

tower-fortress stage (after stage 2)

W4- Frosted Glacier 6- Freezing Rain Tower / Icicle Tower (63,64)

(Icicles rain supreme in this level including the giant ones. Avoid them at all cost. The little ones shatter but the big ones can be use as platforms. If I didn't know any better, I swear that they borrowed this level from the first Megaman game for the Gameboy, play Iceman's stage in that game and you'll know what I'm talking about. Back to the guide. Make your way upwards and kill the Dry Bones if you have ice power on you. The early giant icicles only fall when you reach the wall and won't harm you. There is one part where two giant ones will stack up on top of each other to reach the tilting platform. Another giant icicle is stopped by a blue block. There goes Star Coin #1. Get it safely then run back carefully as the icicles fall then hit the checkpoint flag.

Get on the rising platform and stay ahead of it to get Star Coin #2. Use your ice powers on the Dry Bones. You will come across a part where coins will lead to the right and tell you to wall jump but ignore those and go into the hidden wall on the left and get Star Coin #3. The rising platform will fill up with Dry Bones. It's best to bop the POW Block to kill everything then enter the door. Boom Boom hops then does an air spin attack. He adds more hops before doing the spin. Three hits and he is outta here.)

W4- Frosted Glacier 7- Swinging Ghost House (65,66)

(Once again, the tail attack is truly missed. The door that you have to go through is behind the wall of bricks. The screen will scroll back and forth. To get out of this first area, let it scroll to the right and jump over the wall. Get the powerup if needed then hit the P-Switch. Be sure to leap over Boo and this time run back into the wall to get Star Coin #1 as the bricks hidden in the wall are now coins. You can always hit the P-switch again to turn the wall of bricks into coins then enter the door to move on. The screen scrolls up and down. Get past the Boo and the door you want to enter is the bottom one when the bricks scroll to them and get several coins then get out. Go to the top door next. When the screen scrolls to the right. Hit the P-switch to get several more coins then exit out the door that was on the bottom when you came in as the bricks are now coins and vice versa so you can get in. The coins flee from you. Hit the P-switch and follow them to the end and you leap over the Boos and get Star Coin #2 at the top of the bricks. Enter the door at the end. You are back in the previous room. The door to enter is hidden underneath the one next to the P-switch. In this next room, you will see several doors. Hot the P-switch and you can go through the wall on the very left for a ? switch that points to the correct path which is the door hidden under the P-switch. Now you are in a room where you must hit a P-switch that turns the coins to bricks and you can climb to the top just by jumping because the bricks will follow you and keep you from falling down. The door is at the top, but watch out for Circling Boos and Big Boos then enter the door and proceed to the exit.

Note: You are probably wondering about Star Coin #3. Read on to find out how to get it.

There is a secret exit that leads to Frosted Glacier-Fliprus: Fliprus Lake. To reach it, there is a hidden spot in the ceiling just above the actual exit door. In here, hit the P-switch to change all the coins to bricks and vice versa and quickly head to the right and wall jump up the bricks to get Star Coin #3 then enter the door below to get to the secret exit. Just watch out for the Boo and Giant Boo. Pick up the Spring if you want the 1-up at the end.)

secret stage

W4- Frosted Glacier 8- Fliprus Lake / Fliprus Floes (67,68)

(Note: Completion of this level leads to an early trip to Rock Candy Mines.)

This is the only level where the Flipruses appear. They are Walruses that hurl avalanche snowballs at you. You can stomp on the snowballs to get rid of them. Flipruses can be defeat the conventional way of a good ol' stomp or other means. You will also meet the River Piranha Plants in this level (they debuted in NSMB Wii). They blow spike green balls in the air similar to the Ptooies from SMB3. If the ball is defeated, the RPPs will panic in a sweat as they are powerless. In this level, the Flipruses can also kill them with their snowballs if one should run into them. When you get to a spot where there is a Koopa Troopa on the bricks, jump on the bricks once it's out of the way and then jump up from there for Star Coin #1. When you see a Fliprus just below the thin platform, freeze it and use it for leverage to reach it then enter the pipe. Kill the Flipruses and get Star Coin #2 then exit out of the yellow pipe. Once out, take out the next Fliprus to the right and Ground Pound the crates it was on to make it sink then go right into a secret area that holds a 1-up in a brick. Next to the next Fliprus is another set of crates. Wait for it to rise up quickly and jump at the apex of it's ascent to get a high boost to the upper-right and get Star Coin #3. Bricks will form and you can get the 1-up easily.

Note: Completion of this level leads to an early trip to Rock Candy Mines.)

castle stage

W4- Frosted Glacier 9- Wendy's Shifting Castle / Wendy's Thwomp Castle (69,70)

(This castle consists or girders that shift positions so be careful with your footing to survive this first part as you get several coins. When you see a line of Thwomps and Thwimps including the Giant Thwomp. Just make a run for it. Stop at the last Thwomp and let it drop so you can get Star Coin #1 with a safe wall jump. Then proceed forward to the checkpoint flag. Now you got to deal with swinging girders in combination with the Thwomps and Thwimps with a few Dry Bones added to the mix. You will see two ? blocks ahead with Thwimps jumping over them. There is a hidden spot underneath the second one with coins. Jump on the second block then jump straight up to reveal a hidden coin block then get on top of that one and get into the pipe. Carefully avoid the Thwimps to get Star Coin #2 then safely get out. You will see a green pipe. Step on the part of the girder above it and then let it dump you on top of it and go in. Let the Giant Thwomp drop then safely get Star Coin #3 then exit. Now quickly make a break for the exit door as the Giant Thwomps come crashing down. Let the coins be your guide. The only thing dangerous about this boss fight with Wendy are the icicles above which should not even come into play as you can defeat her with ease. Stomp on her as you avoid the two rings she sends out and watch her do the spinning shell routine then stomp her again as she recovers. That is all you must do.)

W5- Soda Jungle

The Soda Jungle name was derived from soda as a reference to the poison in the world. Ways to enter: completing the castle level in W3- Sparkling Waters or W4- Frosted Glacier, or completing W1- Acorn Plains and W2- Layer-Cake Desert's secret levels, which makes them world-skipping shortcuts. The W5- Soda Jungle also leads to every world afterward besides W8- Peach's Castle and W9- Superstar Road.

12 levels or stages and 3 Toad Houses: 1 green and 2 red

airship stage

[Mario side / Luigi side (exit-level count)]

W5- Soda Jungle 1- Airship The Mighty Cannonship / All Aboard! (71,72)

(Before you get a chance to tackle the Soda Jungle, Bowser's airship will nab you and you get to take on Bowser Jr. at the end of the level. Avoid the Cannonballs and you can use the Mecha-Koopas as weapons against others. Stop them then pick them up and throw them. This is how you defeat Bowser in Super Mario World. Jump up and down on the screws to make them move. You'll be dump through if you stand on them too long without jumping. Climb up the rope ladder then down the other one to get Star Coin #1. Climb back up and continue forward. Use the Giant Cannonball for leverage to get Star Coin #2 then hit the checkpoint flag.

Enter the red pipe to go underwater. You will meet the Red Torpedo Ted that act like homing torpedos. Once they go past you, they'll stop and attack towards your current location until they hit something (hopefully not you) or if they stay in motion too long, they'll explode. You can use them to break the bricks surrounding Star Coin #3 then carefully make it to the pipe at the end.

You can't stop on Bowser Jr since you are underwater but if you remember playing Sonic & Knuckles and got to the Doomsday Zone, you'll get a sense of deja vu here as the first part of that battle is fought the same way here. Bowser Jr. will send out a Red Torpedo Teds and your goal is to lure them to hit him. After the first hit, he will send out regular Torpedo Teds horizontally then another Red Torpedo Ted. After the second hit, the regular ones come in vertically. Now you just need to hit him once more to end the fight.)

7 regular levels

W5- Soda Jungle 2- Jungle of the Giants / Giant Swing-Along (73,74)

(Another blast from the past as you take on giant versions of old foes just as you did in Giant Land in SMB3. Just like in that same game, the bricks and blocks are large too. Stomping on the Grand Goombas splits them into two Mega Goombas and stomping a Mega Goomba splits them into regular Goombas. Four fireballs are needed to kill a Grand Goomba. Giant Koopa Troopas can bounce off the big bricks and they'll smash through small ones. When you reach the second powerup (A red Koopa Troopa is walking on the bricks), stomp on that Koopa Troopa and knock it to the right to smash that first big block then continue to the right and stomp on the next Koopa Troopa and kick it to the right and it'll smash through all the small bricks and give access to Star Coin #1. If you get to see bricks covering a pipe, smash them with a Giant Koopa Shell and go down. There is a P-switch to make several coins appear. You must use the wall kick on the pipes to get them all. Exit out of the right pipe and hit the checkpoint flag.

Make your way to the right until you see a Giant Koopa Troopa on a smaller pipe and knock it away. Go inside and hit the P-switch and watch out for the Grand Goomba and wall kick to get Star Coin #2. You will eventually come across a giant Green Koopa Troopa and use its shell to smash the small bricks and inside the second ? block is an invincibility star, now make a mad dash for the exit goal as you smash through all enemies. You will get Star Coin #3 and as an added bonus, 1-up on the exit goal if you are high enough.)

W5- Soda Jungle 3- Bridge over Poisoned Waters / Dancing Blocks, Poison Swamp (75,76)

(Soda Jungle is like a foreign country, enjoy the scenery but don't drink the water. That goes double here because the purple water is poisonous and results in instant death the moment you fall in just like if it was lava. Get the Super Acorn out of the ? block at the start of the level, you'll need it for one of the Star Coins. Don't stay still on the logs for too long or it will roll you into the deadly waters. You can run across them without worry about that, it's only when you stay still that they'll roll you. You will spot Star Coin #1 and on a log. Get a clear path then jump on the log it is on then go to left to get it. Now go to the right and use a glide jump to enter the pipe above. You can use a glide jump to get Star Coin #2 or you can make use of the POW Block and knock all the coins down and get them all (at least the ones that were visible at the time). You can also hit one brick for a P-switch and use the bricks for leverage to the coin and the blocks. Head to the checkpoint flag on your right.

The road to Star Coin #3 is dangerous. You'll get to it by carefully jumping on sets of dual bricks that move in and move out. One false move will be your doom. Carefully, step onto the shifting block sets and towards the end, if you got the Flying Squirrel suit to catch the coins and hit the exit pole. There is a secret exit that leads to Soda Jungle-6: Seesaw Bridge. To reach it, there is a ? block hanging over the poisoned water towards the end. Use a Koopa Shell to hit it and make the vine rise to the top. If you got a Flying Squirrel suit, get to high ground and glide your way to the secret exit pole.)

W5- Soda Jungle 4- Bramball Woods / Heart of Bramball Woods (77,78)

(The Bramballs will be all over this level. They are not really harmful, they are more like pests. When you step on certain spots, it will form bricks for them to walk on. A hidden 1-up is somewhere to the left of the first ? blocks. Stomp on one of the Bramballs to get inside the pipe above. This contains an ice flower you can to freeze the Bramballs to use as good platforms to reach others out of reach. You'll need to slide down the bricks to get Star Coin #1 then wall jump out. Star Coin #2 is shortly afterwards. Freeze a Bramball below and use it as a stepstool to get to a thin platform and enter a hidden area with Star Coin #2 in it then hit the checkpoint flag. Freeze the Stalking Piranha Plants as they stretch their necks out and gather the green ring and get the green coins for a 1-up. You will eventually come across Star Coin #3 on the bottom. Freeze the Bramballs to keep them from interfering as you use the Donut Lifts to get down there. Just be sure to land on top of the blue blocks to avoid falling into the abyss. After you get the Star Coin, you'll see a pipe for mini Mario and a normal sized pipe. I wonder what's behind that mini pipe. For now take the pipe on the bottom and go for the exit.)

Two of the regular stages are in the inner, haunted (ghost house) area and can only happen after completing the Boo enemy ghost house level of W5- Soda Jungle 5- Which-Way Labyrinth

W5- Soda Jungle 5- Which-Way Labyrinth / Boo's Favorite Haunt (79,80)

(There are five doors at the start of the level. What we want is to go in the one on the far right so you can get the yellow Baby Yoshi. The light it emits will confuse the Scaredy Rats and make them run in the opposite direction they were traveling. You can hit the P-switch for lots of blue coins. Exit out the door to the left and you are back at the start. Enter the upper right door and let the Broozer smash the blocks out of its way on the lower left so you can get Star Coin #1 then jump back to the top through the ceiling. Watch out for the barrels that the other Broozers knock at you. Broozers can be defeated with three stomps. You can stomp them three times in rapid succession. With yellow Yoshi's power you can knock them over and stomp them once to kill them. Now stay on the middle crate to make it lower and enter the door on the bottom right before it sinks into the poisonous water. Go back into the far right door and head back to the exit door except this time jump into the wall past the door and go around and enter the door. Run up the staircase then up the left staircase. The baby Yoshi can eat Boos. At the wall, jump up to reveal a hidden coin block then use it for leverage and jump to the left through the wall and enter the door. Hit the P-switch to reverse the coin and bricks to clear the path to get Star Coin #2 then exit out the lower right door. Run up the first staircase again and enter the door. Let the crate lower as you have baby Yoshi eat the Boos but watch out for the Giant Boo. Baby Yoshi's power can drive it back. You can finish off the remaining ones with the invincibility star then fall to the bottom and enter the door. Exit straight ahead.

There is a secret exit that leads to Soda Jungle-ParaBeetle: Flight of the Para-Beetles. To reach it, go inside the far left door and ride the crate to the top. Don't enter the door though, stay on it to left side just past the door and there is a secret spot in the ceiling that leads to another door to the upper right. Once inside, the floor segments will vanish one by one. Hug the right wall and you will eventually go through the wall and get Star Coin #3. Fall safely to the bottom and enter the door. The secret exit is straight ahead.)

W5- Soda Jungle 6- Painted Swampland / Painted Pipeworks (81,82)

(Stay out of the water as you run through the tilted pipes. Go down the first straight pipe you see which should be gold and wait for an opening inside the Circling Boo Buddies and grab Star Coin #1 then go out through the same pipe. The next straight pipe has Star Coin #2 over it. Jump to get it the moment you step on the pipe as the pipe will sink into the water then grab the checkpoint flag.

Run through the wall to the right and get a 1-up inside the hidden area. Jump through the openings in the Circling Boo Buddies as you proceed. Star Coin #3 is within the 2nd set. Gather the red ring and coins and carefully hop across the pipes to the exit.

There is a secret exit that leads to Soda Jungle-6: Seesaw Bridge. To reach it, there is a spot after you've collected all the red rings. Drop down onto the slanted green pipe below and go into the pocket. There is a hidden pipe that leads to another pipe. The secret exit pole is ahead.)

W5- Soda Jungle 7- Deepsea Ruins / Deepsea Stone-Eyes (83,84)

Either of normal stages 6 or 7 require an (alternate exit) because a (normal exit) otherwise loops back to the (stage 5 ghost house)

(Jump onto the stone heads and you will see Star Coin #1 in the water. Get it then carefully jump through the Circling Boo Buddies then swim into the pipe. The Jellybeams will light up the water as you swim. They can still hurt you when they touch you.

The Bulbers serve the same function in the next area. Swim your way upward past the Circling Boo Buddies, Bulbers, and Fishbones. Star Coin #2 is surrounded by some of the Circling Boo Buddies. At the top watch out for the stone head that knocks you down on the left then let the one on the right fall into place. Star Coin #3 is behind where it used to be. Go up the top pipe. Jump through the tops of the stone heads and hit the exit pole.

There is a secret exit that leads to W5- Soda Jungle 8- Seesaw Bridge. To reach it, go through the pipe just after Star Coin #3 and it leads to the secret exit.)

Back out of the inner haunted area, the final 2 of the regular stages must be completed in sequence.

W5- Soda Jungle 8- Seesaw Bridge / Sumo Bro Bridge (85,86)

(If it ain't our buddy Wiggler coming to greet us. Always remember to defeat him by other means than stomping on him or he will blow his top. This first one you can bop from below and get the powerup. Grab a Kooba shell and use it clear out a few Wigglers then drop down at the coin block and go left and jump up to go through the wall and go down the pipe. I suggest having the Flying Squirrel suit here because getting Star Coin #1 is very dangerous here. Get the coin and get out. Make your way past Wigglers and use the River Piranha Plants. Be sure to grab a Koopa Shell as you will need it to snag Star Coin #2 which is in the poison waters. There is also a 1-up in the block above it. Let the River Piranha Plants retract their spike balls before proceeding then hit the red ring and get red coins and touch the checkpoint flag.

Carefully make your way past the seesaws and slide down the slope to take out three Koopa Troopas. Go down the pipe with the ? block above it. Hit the P-switch and start making a few hidden coins appear above then jump up through the left side and use the blocks to get Star Coin #3 and then drop down and go up the left pipe. Safely get past two rotating seesaws and head to the exit.)

W5- Soda Jungle 9- Wiggler Stampede / Wiggler Floodlands (87,88)

(Unlike their smaller counterparts, Giant Wigglers don't go ballistic if you stop on them. You can use them for trampolines. The second one will give you leverage to reach Star Coin #1. Bounce off it to get safely out the pit then go right. When you get to around the third one. Use it to hit the middle brick to make a vine rise. This leads to a secret section where you can make more vines rise and climb up to get Star Coin #2. Hit the checkpoint flag when you come back down. Jump on the Giant Wiggler to hit the P-switch. This Wiggler will be your buddy for the rest of the level. Use it get to all the coins you can gather and hit another P-switch after the first one expires. Eventually, you will have to jump onto a platform as your buddy submerges then wait for your buddy to emerge. If you end up getting the star out the item box, wait for it to wear off before you jump on it again or you'll kill it and you via poison water. Jump on the next mushroom platform and either use the glide jump to get Star Coin #3. Ride your buddy all the way to the exit. or wait for your buddy to emerge.)

tower stage (after stage 4)

W5- Soda Jungle 10- Snake Block Tower / Stone-Snake Tower (89,90)

(Get the powerup out of the bricks if needed and go into the pipe. Ride on the snake block as you avoid the swinging chain balls, Amps, and Big Amps. Use a careful jump to get Star Coin #1. As you ride up, you will see a smaller version of the snake blocks to the upper left making its way up. There is Star Coin #2 there. Jump back onto the big snake block after collecting the coins and go into the pipe. The checkpoint flag will fall down before you go inside if you want to hit it. You will need some careful jumps to get past the swinging chains and Big Amps as you try to stay on the snake block then jump to the small one to reach Star Coin #3 and then jump back over the Big Amp and continue to ride the big snake block until you reach the top. Crouch to avoid the swinging chains and go into the door on the top left of the level. Boom Boom will grow to large size but he is still go down in three hits. His first attack is a helicopter spin. Stomp him and he will use stomps then flail his arms and charge for the next two hits.)

W5- Soda Jungle 11- Flight of the Para-Beetles / Para-Beetle Parade (91,92)

(Note: Completion of this level leads to an early trip to W7- Meringue Clouds.)

This section is full of Para-Beetles and giant ones. As usual, they may be enemies in the game but they'll always be your buddies in the same role that Giant Wiggler, Jellybeam, Bulber, etc. played in the game as they give you a hand and only hurt you if you touch them the wrong way. Jumping on the regular Para-Beetles will make them rise up slowly. Jumping on the giant ones called Heavy Para-Beetles, they will slowly sink. Jumping on eight Para-Beetles without touching the ground will make a 1-up appear. Star Coin #1 can be reached by jumping on the first heavy one followed by the next three regular ones . Jump on the last one in line to get a rise to the next set and a powerup. Jump to the end of the line and jump the next line of Para-Beetles to the left. Then get the red ring and get the red coins from the tops of the four Heavy Para-Beetles and just jump on the first regular Para-Beetle to get to the platform. You will meet King Bill. This enemy is going to be a nightmare because it is invincible. Have a Flying Squirrel suit and use it to get Star Coin #2 then glide jump to the left and go up before King Bill gets you. You will also have to avoid one coming down vertically on the right. The coins actually warn you about King Bill coming by forming into the shape of them wherever they are gonna come. From the next platform, hit the P-switch to form more warning coins temporarily. When you get to the final four Para-Beetles. Let King Bill pass then manipulate one of the Para-Beetles to use as a platform to get into the red pipe. Here you can get Star Coin #3 and use the Heavy Para-Beetle to get to the exit at a high point. Note: Completion of this level leads to an early trip to Meringue Clouds.)

W5- Soda Jungle 12- Iggy's Volcanic Castle / Iggy's Swinging-Chains Castle (93,94)

(The floor will rise up and down. The lava will move in waves and they will kill you on the spot as if you fell into the lava yourself. Use careful jumping to avoid them. Get an Ice Flower and Freeze one of the Dry Bones when on higher ground to knock out several more including a giant one. Bear in mind that if a frozen Dry Bones touches the lava, it will thaw out and stay alive. Star Coin #1 is visible. Get it in-between waves. Head for the checkpoint flag just ahead.

When you see two overhead green pipes, use a Dry Bones for leverage to get inside the second one. Throw down the POW block in this room to knock down Star Coin #2 and all other coins here then exit out. Now jump through Giant Dry Bones and Podobos and when you get to the golden pipe, wait for the waves to be at a low point and enter the green pipe. It's kinda dangerous but bounce off the Giant Dry Bones to get Star Coin #3 then exit out and enter the door.

Iggy is one slick character just like his stage. He will retreat in one of the four pipes and come out in a random one. He will shoot a trio of magic beams. The red ones will spawn a giant Magmaargh if it touches the lava and you got to avoid it at all costs. The part that makes Iggy a pain is that when you stomp him. Rather than move back and forth in his shell along the walls, he will double back and come at you or double back and retreat into the pipe to try to get you from the other side. He needs to be taken out as quickly as possible. Three good stomps and he's gone.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines

The Rock-Candy Mines are entered by clearing Soda Jungle's castle, or by completing the secret worlds in Frosted Glacier and Sparkling Waters.

10 levels include 7 regular levels or stages

[Mario side / Luigi side (exit-level count)]

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 1- Fuzzy Clifftop / Mount Fuzzy (95,96)

(Meet Fuzzy. It is furball with a happy face that moves along whatever line it touches. The first one is above you and that will eventually get caught in a loop. The ? block by the loop contains Yoshi. Move to the right and eat two Fuzzies. You'll need the other Fuzzy to bounce on and obtain Star Coin #1. Throughout the stage you will come across blocks that expand into multiple blocks when they move down and retract into single blocks when they move up. Stay clear of the Fuzzies as you move and touch the checkpoint flag.

When you reach the windmill drop down and hover to the pipe on the lower left and go down the pipe. Bounch off the Fuzzies below to get Star Coin #2 while avoiding the Fuzzy above then get out. Go left into the hidden wall and go up and back on the windmill. You will meet the Venus Ice Trap in this level. You can swallow it or it's ice balls and spit out ice balls to freeze anyone in its path. Star Coin #3 is guarded by several Piranha Plants. He the ones on top and bounce off the bottom ones and get the coin. Now it's a matter of getting through the Fuzzies and "I'll call them elastic blocks". With Yoshi, you can eat the Fuzzies. Enter the pipe at the end. The exit is straight ahead.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 2- Porcupuffer Falls / Porcu-Puffer Cavern (97,98)

(The level name already tells you that Porcupuffer will be harassing you in this level. It is only a pain if you are on the surface of the water. Below the surface and it won't be a bother. You can knock it out of the way temporarily then it will come back after a number of seconds. When you get to the wall, jump up to reveal a hidden block and use it to get over the wall and drop down to get Star Coin #1. Get put of the water before Porcupuffer comes back. Dip into the next pool and collect the red ring and coins. Knock out the Porcupuffer again and hit the checkpoint flag.

Have Koopa or Paratroopa shell with you and go swimming. You need the shell to knock out three Urchins and get Star Coin #2 then swim upward and to the right and get on the Donut Lifts. There are only coins below them. To get Star Coin #3, jump onto the item block then jump up to make a vine appear. Climb up to a secret area with coins then drop down to the right and Star Coin #3 is ready to collect. Now just enter the exit pipe to the right and on to the exit.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 3- Waddlewing's Nest / Spike's Seesaws (99,100)

(Waddlewings get a level for themselves. At the start, do a Ground Pound on the yellow nail to free the Chain Chomp and Ground Pound the bricks to go in the wall past it for free coins. Make your way up the tilting platforms and beware of the Piranha Plants. You want to jump onto the red pipe and go down. Ground Pound down the second row of bricks and get Star Coin #1 and get out once you reach the bottom. As you continue back upward, you may notice a Waddlewing fly through the wall. That's a clue to go inside yourself and there is a P-switch. Hit it and you'll see blue coins leading somewhere. Follow them and you'll end up in a wall and get a boost from the blocks and you will get Star Coin #2 here. Get to top and hit the checkpoint flag.

Enter the pipe to the right. Ride on the platform as it falls. Avoid being hit by Waddlewings during the descent. You will have a chance to wall jump to get Star Coin #3. Knock out the Chain Chomp nails once you reach the bottom and enter the pipe leading to the end of the level.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 4- Light Blocks, Dark Tower / Light-Up-Lift Tower (101,102)

(Another piece of innovation for the NSMB series. The level is dark with Swoopers and the blocks will light up and darken in spots. A good thing to know is that you can maintain invincibility throughout the left if you are fast enough. The first star is at the start of the level. Get it and the next ? blocks you see will have stars if you are still in Invincibility mode. Star Coin #1 is in plain sight. Maintain your invincibility until you get to a spot below a golden pipe. You don't want to go in there while invincible because you need those Koopa Paratroopas to get Star Coin #2 then get out. Go to the top of the level and enter the pipe and get the checkpoint flag inside.

Try not to get blown up by the Bob-ombs as you hit them with fireballs to light them up faster. Hit the ? switch on the ceiling to light up all blocks. You'll need a Bob-omb to blow away the bricks blocking the gold pipe. Enter inside and hava another blow up the box at the end for a 1-up then make it to the top and get rid of the Fire Bros. especially the one below Star Coin #3 and go into the green pipe below exit the level.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 5- Walking Piranha Plants! / Rising Piranhas (103,104)

(Swing on the chain and jump on the rock as it tilts and jump off before they fall. Use the Koopa shell to knock out a lot of Stalking Piranha Plants and go to the bottom and enter the wall and get Star Coin #1 hidden inside. You will have to a running slide to get under the top brick if you are a big Mario. Swing across several chains until you reach a spot with a Super Acorn in it if you are Super Mario. Get the Acorn and go back to the left and do a glide jump by the upper wall and you'll be in a secret area. Hit the P-switch and get on the bricks and glide jump to Star Coin #2. Drop down to the right and continue swinging to the right and hit the continue flag.

You'll see Star Coin #3 and you'll have to do a well-timed glide jump to get it then wall jump to get back up to safety. You can get an Ice Flower out of the spot where dropped down prior to getting the Star Coin and go right this time. Use the Koopa Shell or Ice Flower to defeat all SPPs on route to the exit.

There is a secret exit that leads to the use of another switch instead of the level. You'll get to it by getting to the final chain in the level then go left instead as there is a pipe hidden in the wall that leads to the secret exit.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 6- Thrilling Spine Coaster / Spine Coaster Stowaways (105,106)

(Time for a wild ride on the spinecoaster. Too bad it has nothing on the DKC rides. One thing you'll love about this ride is that it will warn you if it's going to dip into the poisonous waters. You will see Star Coin #1 along the way. That's the only 1 of 2 times it'll roar without dipping into the death pool. Get the red ring and gather all the red coins. When the ride starts slowing down, hit the ? switch and get all the coins you can while the purple blocks are solid then hop back on the ride. It'll roar again but don't worry about it. Get the invincibility star out the ? block as you will be killing Spike Tops. Get ready to snag Star COin #2 in the air after the invincibility wears off then avoid the poison waters then get another star. Make it to the end and hit the ? block quick for another star and enter the pipe. You need one more star to run across the Munchers to get Star Coin #3 then run back. Ride one more spine coaster to the exit. The top one can help you get higher.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 7- Shifting Floor Cave / Switch-Lift Express (107,108)

(Bop the Spike Tops from below before they turn the corner then enter the pipe. Take out another Spike Top and a couple swoopers as you make your way through shifting floors. Be careful where you stand because some floors can dump you into the abyss if you stand on them too long. Some will even steer you into a Piranha Plant. Star Coin #1 can be obtained by waiting for the floor to get underneath it before grabbing it then moving on before you fall. Wait for the floor to stretch out and run across to the checkpoint flag because jumping is a bad idea with the Giant Piranha Plant above.

Bop a few for Spike Tops from below then get rid of a Swooper and ride a floor to the top and get over the ceiling where there are lots of coins and Star Coin #2 up there to the right. There is an invincibility star in one of the bricks above the Koopa Troopa below. Do a ground pound to start hitting the bricks and spare one of the Koopa Troopas in that area. You'll need it's shell to get Star Coin #3. In the meantime clear out any enemies you can first then go back for the shell and get the coin and get on top of the pipe as the floor retracts then enter the pipe when it comes back. Onward to the exit.)

tower 1 stage (after stage 2)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 8- Grinding-Stone Tower / Smashing-Stone Tower (109,110)

(Make your way up as you avoid the grinding rocks and Dry Beetles. The latter will occasionally bear their spikes and make it dangerous to jump on them. When you see a pipe moving forward and back, get on top of it and go through the wall behind it and it will lead to a Mini Mushroom. Now carefully get past the grinding rocks and run up the wall into the mini-pipe. Get past the giant grinding rock and get Star Coin #1 then run up the wall to get out. Star Coin #2 is located in a hidden wall. What you do is the moment you get out of the pipe and wait for the grinding rock to go to the very left and you can just run up the wall and into the wall with Star Coin #2 and hit the continue flag from there.

Get the mushroom to get big again then hop up safely and go into the wall for the red ring then collect the red coins. Turns out that the grinding stones can be bopped from below. Work your way up as you get through grinding stones and moving pipes. This reminds me so much of a level from Battletoads. Once you make it to the top, go inside the door to face Boom Boom.

Boom Boom sprouts wings just like he did in SMB3 in some castles. Just stomp on him when he swoops down at you. He gets more vicious with each stomp and he'll die in three hits. There is a secret exit that leads to Rock Candy Mines-6: Thrilling Spine Coaster. To reach it, stay as Mini Mario until you reach close to the top and you'll see a mini pipe. Wait for a grinding rock to spawn then run into the pipe before the next one spawns. Carefully make it to the top and get Star Coin #3 and enter the pipe leading to the secret exit.)

tower 2 stage (after stage 6)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 9- Screwtop Tower / Sumo Bro's Spinning Tower (111,112)

(Get on the Screwtop and do the Spin Jump to make the platform move underneath the red pipe and enter. Get past the Dry Bettles and spin on the screw platform and spin on it. Spin on another screw platform and hit the two hidden coins by the gold pipe and let the platform spin back and enter the pipe. Jump on a safe spot on the blocks and boost to the platforms above and throw down the POW block to knock down all coins including Star Coin #1. Climb up and spin up the right platform to get coins then jump to the left to spin up the other one. Bop that Sumo Bro from below or he'll give you hell. Get past a couple firebars and hit the checkpoint flag.

Continue upward and carefully ride the screw platform as the firebar spins around. Use a frozen enemy to take out a Sumo Bro then spin your way to Star Coin #2. The next Sumo Bro you can freeze and smash. Make your way up the right side and go to the left and ride the screw platform to the end of its point and jump up. Try to get the red rings and coins if you don't mind the risk. Knock out or kill the Dry Beetles and ride the screw platform past the dual firebars. Get rid of the Sumo Bro and make the invisible coins blocks going up to the ceiling and get Star Coin #3 then enter the door.

You don't fight Boom-Boom here. You fight a giant Sumo Bro. Bop it from below and then stomp on its belly. Do this three times and the fight is over. You only got to avoid the lightning from its stomps.)

W6- Rock-Candy Mines 10- Roy's Conveyor Castle / Roy's Ironclad Castle (113,114)

(Note: You cannot grab all three Star Coins in one shot. The final one requires you use the switches on the map to reach the back door.)

Wait for the blocks to fall into the lava to use as platforms. When going for Star Coin #1, let the first block fall then rush over to collect it before the next block falls and seal off access to it. Ride on the blocks across the lava and duck down if the blocks are tall to get under the gap. Be sure to go up both pockets here. The first one has a lot of coins and the other one has a pipe to go up in. Quickly make a break for Star Coin #2 before that block falls on it. The next brick has a 1-up. Hit the checkpoint flag.

All you have to do for this next part is hit the ? switch and all the blocks above will rain down and crush all of the Dry Bones to death. Enter the door from there.

Roy brings a Bazooka to the fight and shoots Bullet Bills. There are mini-airships in the air for standing room. Get the first hit in and this fight is yours. Let him do his routine which last longer than some and hit him as he recovers. If he gets off an attack after the second hit, he will do a Ground Pound that sends Bullet Bills in two directions.

You must go through the back door to get Star Coin #3. Head to the left and step on the ? block to make the blocks rain down and quickly get the Star Coin before it is sealed off. From there you can ride on the blocks and jump up and enter the door leading to Roy Koopa.)

W7- Meringue Clouds

The Meringue Clouds is a sky world accessed by completing the castle level of W6- Rock-Candy Mines or completing W5- Soda Jungle's secret level.

10 levels, include six regular stages

[Mario side / Luigi side (exit-level count)]

W7- Meringue Clouds 1- Land of the Flying Blocks / Frozen Fuzzies (115,116)

(Get past a gang of Waddlewings and get the coins. Get on the cloud and it will start moving to the right. During your travels, one block will have a trampoline. Use the trampoline to reach a red pipe that has no Piranha Plant coming out of it. Go inside that pipe and the bricks will start to form a bridge that guide you to Star Coin #1 and then exit out the pipe. Star Coin #2 is right there just as you drop down. Let the bricks form so you can get to it easier. At the end of the ride, head for the green pipe at the end of the line and hit the checkpoint flag.

Ride two moving clouds as you avoid Waddlewings and Super Piranha Plants. Bricks will start forming in and out and when you see Star Coin #3, use a ground pound to get it as the bricks try to block it. Past the string of SPPs, the exit is right ahead.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 2- Seesaw Shrooms / Wiggler Rodeo (117,118)

(Run to the right and get the Fire Flower to take care of the Fuzzies. Get Yoshi and do a hover jump to the lower platform to the right to get Star Coin #1. Eat your way to the right and hit the checkpoint flag.

Watch out for Lakitu and the Spiny Eggs he throws that turn into Spinies. If you can, stomp on him and highjack his cloud the first chance you get and Star Coin #2 is just ahead. Highjack another cloud to give you some ground to cover. Bounce off the Fuzzies to get into that pipe on top. Jump off Yoshi to get Star Coin #3. Get back on and exit out. The exit flag is shortly ahead. Just a couple Fuzzies to get past.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 3- Switchback Hill / Rainbow Skywalk (119,120)

(The gimmick for this level is the switchback platforms that travel in the direction the arrow on it is pointing. Avoid the Bullet Bills by ducking. Use this to get Star Coin #1. There are also spots where you'll have to duck under the walls. One particular spot has a hidden item box where you can jump on the lower switchback and ride it down then jump to the left to hit it. Ride over the Bullet Bill launcher and get on the next switchback and jump up at the wall and there is a hidden pipe in the ceiling to go in. Avoid the Bullet Bills as you guide the switchback to Star Coin #2 then go back down the pipe and hit the checkpoint flag.

Get the Ice Flower and jump across the switchbacks. Ride down the fourth one and go into the wall at the bottom and get coins and go back out. Grab the POW block and smash it when underneath a switchback you can reach. Star Coin #3 will fall on it. Ride the other switchbacks to keep up with it and once it reaches the end of its ride wait for it to fall and snag it. All that's left is avoid the enemies and exit the level.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 4- Bouncy Cloud Boomerangs / Above the Bouncy Clouds (121,122) (Get past the first few Green Koopa Paratroopas then use the bouncy clouds to get past a set of Goombas. You will see the first boomerang brother. Avoid the boomerangs he throws then stomp him to get him out of your way. See that pit covered in clouds prior to the Boomerang Brother? You want to slide down the pipe where the pit is and gather Star COin #1 then hop your way out and proceed to the right. You will see several Green Koopa Paratroopas and several bricks and ? blocks. Find a spot to break through the bricks via Ground Pound and land on the clouds below. Bop the ? blocks and one of them will reveal a giant vine (Middle one to be exact) leading to a secret area. Bounce along the clouds to reach a POW block. Grab it and toss it to the ground to make several coins fall to get Star Coin #2. Leave the area and go right again. Get the red ring and red coins while avoiding the Goombas who also bounce on the clouds then hit the checkpoint flag.

Get the ice flower if you want it then avoid the Boomerang brother's boomerangs and bounce to get the final Star Coin. Now it is a matter of getting past the piranha plants and Goombas but fortunately for you, you will come across a star to get you through the rest of the level safely if you are fast enough.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 5- A Quick Dip in the Sky / Flame Chomp Ferris Wheel (123,124)

(It's time to make an upward swim using the many bubbles you will see floating in the sky. I admit that this is another great innovation on part of Nintendo and the NSMB series in general. The first power-up you see besides the Super Mushroom (if you are small) is the Fire Flower which will come in handy against the Piranha Plants especially the big ones which you will need to get rid of to get Star Coin #1 more safely. On the way up, there is a spot where you see a lone Red Koopa Troopa and a string of Red Koopa Troopas in an upward slope. Turn the lone one into a shell and safely get to the top and kick it towards the bottom and follow it to get a least one 1-up. Past that area is the spot I mentioned earlier with the Giant Piranha Plants and the first Star Coin. If you lost your firepower, use another nearby Koopa Troopa's shell to take out the bottom one and hang around there to get the coin. Stay within the bubble and use it to reach the midpoint flag.

Swim to the top and watch out for the Piranha Plants coming out of the side red pipes. Kill or carefully avoid the fuzzy and climb up through the left side. There is a hidden wall to the right before reaching the platform. Walk to the right and go under the Koopa Troopa and go down the pipe and it will shoot you through Star Coin #2 and kill a 1-up's worth of Koopa Troopas and Koopa Paratroopas. Get to the rotating bubbles and you will see two Fuzzies rotating around the final star coin. Use Firepower to get rid of them and get the coin. Make your way to that green pipe at the top and enter. You can use the Green Paratrooper to get the top of the flagpole.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 6- Snaking Above Mist Valley / Three-Headed Snake Block (125,126)

(Stay on the snake platform no matter what. Fall off and you die. The Flying Squirrel suit really helps in this level. Hit the P-switch and get the blue coins and the Star Coin #1 at the end of the trail. The second Star Coin is obtainable by riding the block upwards to it. At the end of the ride is a green pipe. Enter it and shoot upwards and then touch the midpoint flag.

You are riding another snake block. Watch out for the Fire Brother's fireballs and bop him from below. You can take the high or the low road. The low road leads to a green ring and green coins. Avoid the Red Paratroopas especially the ones that hide behind the thick clouds. To get the final star coin, you must use a Koopa shell to hit it. You only have two Fire Brothers as major threats after this and once you enter the pipe at the end, you are home free.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 7- Spinning Spirit House / Vanishing Ghost House (127,128)

(Ignore the Boo gang and enter the door. Go inside the right wall and enter the door inside. The house will shift. Don't worry about the first door it is a fake. Go into the second door. Go up the stairs to the left and go into the left door. Stomp Broozer three times after it frees up Star Coin #1 and then collect the latter and enter the door. Now between the two doors is a spring to get on the top floor and enter the right door next and stay between the Circling Boo Buddies and when you go after Star Coin #2, it will fly away from you and go to the upper left side. Collect it and enter the door. Go down the stairs on the very right and enter the right door. Avoid the poltergeist blocks and the Big Boos and enter the door first chance you get. Go ahead and finish the level.

There is a secret exit that leads to an early trip to W7- Meringue Clouds-Castle 9- Ludwig's Clockwork Tower. To get it, when on the top floor run to the left and you'll fall next to a door, make your way down and hit the P-switch for some coins and at the bottom go to the right and get Star Coin #3 then go left and enter the door leading to the secret exit.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 8- Slide Lift Tower / Stonecrush Tower (129,130)

(Avoid the fireballs the Fire Bro throws then go into the pipe on the upper right. Avoid or kill more Fire Bros. as you make your way up using the slide lifts. Get the invincibility star under one Fire Bro and go up as much as you can while invincible. You will see Star Coin #1 above a Fire Bro. Smash the bricks to get it and go up the pipe and touch the checkpoint flag.

Keeping climbing your way up as you avoid the firebars. Glide across a set of coins as there is a pipe hidden inside the wall. Use the Slide Lifts to reach Star Coin #2 then glide out. Get the Fire Flower and continue to go up the right side of the wall by making hidden coins appear then go inside the ceiling where there is a pipe. Use the slide lifts to get up and to the left for Star Coin #3. Don't get crushed. Now jut enter the pipe. You come out next to the door and ready to fight.

Magikoopa will be the sub-boss this time around. He flies high above and shoots magic beams down and turns floor parts into Donut Lifts and send out smaller enemies too. Wait for him to send platforms then step on them to get an advantage against him to stomp on him. Three stomps and he's history.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 9- Ludwig's Clockwork Castle / Ludwig's Block-Press Castle (131,132)

(Ludwig proves his worth as the last Koopaling to defeat. But if you stay on him, he'll fall as easily as his siblings before him. His first attack will be for him to jump into the air in the middle and split into three. Two are illusions. They will shoot 2 beams in a split formation before coming down. Two of them will disappear when damaged but the real one will retreat into his shell when hit and spin back and forth. Don't give him time to fully recover, stomp him again as he gets up as his next attack will have three-way beams (9 total to avoid). His final attack will make the trio shift positions and fire between two and three-way beams. Three hits and he is out.)

W7- Meringue Clouds 10- Boarding the Airship / Bowser Jr. Showdown (133,134)

(You can attack Bowser Jr. whenever he punches at you then run up his arm and stomp on him. Avoid his Bob-ombs while doing so. Three hits and he is gone. If you are fast enough you can also stomp on him as he is charging but it takes good timing to nail him.)

W8- Princess Peach's Castle

Peach's Castle is also known as the Mushroom Castle or Castle Toadstool and is the home of Princess Peach Toadstool and the centerpiece of Toad Town; albeit after Browser took her castle over, he turned it into a volcanic land of falling brimstone and flowing lava, aka, Lethal Lava Land.

Super Mario Odyssey (cross-over)

Spoiler warning: Don't you even dare read the spoiler! Because if you do… Hoo hoo hoo hoo hoooooo… A horrible fate awaits you. (Skip this section)

After rescuing Princess Peach from Bowser in the Moon Kingdom, Mario can travel to the Mushroom Kingdom, where he can enter Princess Peach's castle.

W8- Peach's Castle 1- Meteor Moat (135,136)

(Make your way up and to the right. Watch out for Meteors raining down. They destroy all bricks and blocks in its path and anything connected to it. You will see Star Coin #1 straight ahead. Wait till the platform it is on rise above the lava before you get it then hit the checkpoint flag.

Avoid touching the lava geysers at all cost and Star Coin #2 is surrounded by bricks. Use a Ground Pound to get it but wait for the Dry Beetle be out off the way then slide down to get the coin and quickly get out before the meteors destroy your footing. Continue to the right and make use of those rock platforms in the air. The floor dips up and down and some of it sinks completely into the lava. Star Coin #3 is tough to get. As you wait for the floor to rise out of the lava, wait for the floor to be at its apex before sliding down the wall to get it then quickly get out and head for the exit from there.

There is a secret exit that leads Peach's Castle-4: Firefall Cliffs. You'll get to it by hitting the P-switch some time before getting Star Coin #3 and just ignoring it in favor of getting into the pipe above while the coins are still bricks.)

W8- Peach's Castle 2- Magma River Cruise (137,138)

(Don't dwaddle to long. There is a deadly cloud rushing in from the left and it equals instant death if it touches you. Step onto the platform that serves as a ride across the magma river. It will start with the number 5 but as enemies get onto the ride, the number will decrease and will stop working if it hits 0. Mario and the gang do not count against that number. Clear off some Monty Moles and when you see Star Coin #1, bop the Koopa Troopa from below and get on the block it was on then jump up while on the left block to make an invisible block appear then get on top of it. The blocks from below will shift and appear above for you to get on them and leap to Star Coin #1. Here comes a bunch of Micro Goombas. They can each add against the platform total so kill all you can and then clear all the enemies on the platform ride already to bring it back to 5. Watch out for Magmaws that spawn from the lava. They cannot be defeated so your best bet is to avoid them. When you get to a spot after the next Monty Mole falls, you can get onto the platform it was on then jump off to the right to get coins then drop down to reunite with your platform. There is an Ice Flower in the next ? block. The Magmaws are out in full force so be on your toes. Get rid of a string of Micro Goombas and Buzzy Beetles falling from the ceiling. Don't even think about hitting that P-switch. It will make the Micro Goombas fall down and bring the count down to 0. Break the bricks manually then collect Star Coin #2. Eliminate some Monty Moles and get past two more Magmaws. When you see Star Coin #3, let the far end of the ride, get to it and collect it then hurry back to the other end to enter the red exit pipe. On to the exit.)

W8- Peach's Castle 3- Rising Tides of Lava (139,140)

(Lava will rise and fall in this level. Your "buddies" for this level are the Big Buzzy Beetles. They are immune to lava so you can stand on their shells to protect yourself from the lava. This is crucial to getting Star Coin #1. You will also have to make use of the screwtop platforms. Do a ground pound on the set of bricks when safe and throw a Koopa shell down there when the lava is down and kick it in-between the bricks to make lots of coins be collected. Just after the item box, hit the second brick to make the P-switch appear. Stomp on the Koopa Troopa and step on the switch and throw the shell and you can collect coins by jumping while the Koopa shell collects the rest. The Koopa shell finishes running its course by hitting a block that makes a 1-up appear. After the 1-up, wait for the lava to sink then run down the low road quickly and collect Star Coin #2 and hit the checkpoint flag.

Use the screwtop platform to make the other platform rise then use it to get to the next platform. Wait for the Big Buzzy Beetles to get into position and get across the lava using them as platform. Next, use the screwtop again to make the next platform rise and hit the middle ? block to raise a vine and climb it to a secret area. Jump off the Fire Chomp for leverage to reach Star Coin #3 then drop down. Use the screwtops get to the next safe platform then jump off the Giant Buzzy Beetle to get into the pipe and onward to end the level.)

W8- Peach's Castle 4- Firefall Cliffs (141,142)

(Now it's time to demonstrate your rock climbing skills. Avoid the meteors raining down from above. Whenever you see a set of small rocks bunched together. You can climb through the rocks like they were the chain link fences in the castles. When you come across a POW block smash it anyway you can and Star Coin #1 will fall down. If you get the invincibility star, you can kill meteors as if they are enemies themselves and you can also maintain an invincibility streak as you hit the checkpoint flag.

Climb up the left side of the next past safely and you'll get Star Coin #2 at the top of the second set of rocks. Grab the green ring and green coins and get the 1-up then throw a Koopa shell at the brick to get another 1-up. As the screen scrolls up, climb up through the right side and duck off to the right to avoid the big meteors and at the top is Star Coin #3. Go into the pipe at the end. Watch out as the meteors will destroy the platform pieces as you try to exit.)

W8- Peach's Castle 5- Red Hot Elevator Ride (143,144)

(Get the powerup out of the ? block and enter the pipe. We finally get to make use of the Wii U controller as a motion controller. Jump onto the elevator as you try to stay ahead of the lava. There is a 1 on the elevator. If an enemy lands on it and turn it to 0, it will stop moving. Avoid the sparks coming from the Bowser heads. To get Star Coin #1, it is safe to get yourself smashed against the ceiling without getting crushed to death. It will make the elevator go down temporarily so you can collect it. The next part is best for you to hit the P-switch and gather the coins. If the elevator detects you are not on it, it will come down for you to get back on. Steer through the Bob-ombs and hit the P-switch on the left to free up Star Coin #2. The sparks will travel from right to left so be sure to avoid those. Get the red ring and the red coins will guide your path upwards. Keep the elevator clear of Bob-ombs as you get Star Coin #3 and enter the door. Head straight to the exit.)

W8- Peach's Castle 6- The Final Battle (145,146)

(Bowser Jr. constantly tries to make your life hell. When he is above you he will attempt to ground pound you. If he misses, that will be the least of your problems if he landed on a bone platform as the floor will rise up one by one in both directions. Wait for him to miss a ground pound then slide down the wall to get Star Coin #1 and wall climb back up. Another problem you will have is that if he ground pounds the moving platform, it will sink into the lava. When you see Star Coin #2, let Bowser Jr. smash the bricks then get it as he rises back up. Make a rush to the right and you will see Star Coin #3. Do a wall jump to get if faster and then make a break for the door and enter. Hit the checkpoint flag and enter the door to take on Big Bowser.

Avoid the fireballs coming from the right and you'll come face to face with Bowser. Round 1 is the same as you fought him many times before. Wait for Bowser to jump high into the air and run under him and jump on the switch and he will take a dive into the abyss. You'll see Princess Peach in the background. Bowser grows to an enormous size and Bowser Jr. will try to ground pound you during the fight. Whenever he does, avoid it to make him miss then stomp on him and hijack his copter and fly above Bowser's head and press ZR or shake the Wiimote to do a ground pound of your own. Avoid the spinning shell after you hit him then wait for him to come out of his shell and dodge more fireballs. His next attack consists of him spitting more fireballs into the air and make them rain down on you. Avoid them and the Bob-omb that Bowser Jr. throws down. Hijack Bowser Jr's copter again and hit Bowser again. One more hit and he is finished. Fortunately, you take no damage if you get hit while in the copter. CONGRATS!! YOU BEAT THE GAME!! Keep an eye out later on as I cover Superstar Road.)

Credits

God Almighty - Lord and Savior.

Nintendo - making the game.

You - for reading.

W9- Superstar Road

Superstar Road is a world in New Super Mario Bros. U and New Super Luigi U, after the player finishes the game. If the player gathers all the Star Coins in any other world, then he or she will have access to a level depending on which world. The Toad Houses in this world also contain items that could not be accessible before, the Propeller Mushroom and the Penguin Suit. It is a spiritual successor to the previous secret worlds and Star Roads alike. In New Super Luigi U, the Propeller Mushroom and the Penguin Suit are in regular levels as well.

9 regular levels and four Toad Houses

[Mario side / Luigi side (exit-level count)]

W9- Superstar Road 1- Spine-Tingling Spine Coaster / Spine Coaster Connection (147,148)

W9- Superstar Road 2- Run for It / P Switch Peril (149,150)

W9- Superstar Road 3- Swim for Your Life! / Star Coin Deep Dive (151,152)

W9- Superstar Road 4- Hammerswing Caverns (153,154)

W9- Superstar Road 5- Spinning Platforms of Doom / Under Construction (155,156)

W9- Superstar Road 6- Fire Bar Cliffs / Fire Bar Sprint (157,158)

W9- Superstar Road 7- Latiku! Latiku! Latiku! / Cloudy Capers (159,160)

W9- Superstar Road 8- Pendulum Castle / Impossible Pendulums (161,162)

W9- Superstar Road 9- Follow that Shell! / Flying Squirrel Ovation (163,164)

I did notice that each regular world final level is a fortress or castle that ends with a fight against Bowser or rather one of his minions disguised as him: the seven Koopalings plus Kamek, Nabbit and Browser Jr. Also, one can check one's progress in the game relative to which world (W1- through W8-), and even which stage within that world (1- through 8- or more) that one has finished so far, all in one direct path, until one can finally can finish 8th world and rescue Peach from Browser himself [and then, subsequently, Peach will be able to restore her kingdom of Toad people back to normal. (Since this is the Deluxe version, the ninth world, W9- Superstar Road is an extra world.)

In Odyssey there may be new maneuvers that may be even more difficult (at first) to learn than those in Super Mario and Kart, but the game is quite different. Whereas in Super Mario, successive levels build on the challenges and skills required to complete the prior levels, in Odyssey, the challenge is to discover and explore kingdoms that are open as to what should be accomplished and when. You choose which goals you should tackle – collect something valuable, learn a new ability from the inhabitants of this world, or keep yourself and your friends healthy enough to be able to keep on exploring together. In Odyssey, you choose your goal and switch up what you are trying to do as often and whenever you want or as often as you think is best for you and your friends to have a good time together and learn things together.

In Odyssey the player explores worlds which are in different kingdoms, each on a different celestial body that may orbit a different star (which may even be in a different galaxy.) Any next world or level is not particularly pre-determined, nor sequential. You do not particularly have to finish progressing through each kingdom in a certain order, but you do have to unlock levels to access necessary resources needed to reach other levels. However, above all else, you must be curious, explore, roam around (using "free-roaming gameplay"), to search for and find paths and discover ways to find paths, both within a world or kingdom and between worlds or kingdoms. Notice little things that may turn out to be quite interesting! Try something and find out what happens! Look for, find and discover super cool things! Collect special, maybe even important and valuable things! Do a little side, creative, mini-task or mission (like build a castle or something, out of sand, before someone knocks it down.) Navigational paths, courses, levels, kingdoms, storylines and plots, in other words, the side story for each kingdom and the main story for the entire game, each may perhaps have normal, regular, multiple-exits, that is, various ways to exit and to switch to another path, or to another side story, or to another kingdom, and then, perhaps switch back, perhaps to a checkpoint in a previous kingdom. See if you can discover how to find and enable (or capture) a checkpoint (can you capture the Browser enemy flag and put up your own Mario flag on that flagpole?) You can use the + / - button to see, review and check what you have collected or saved, including checkpoints, and perhaps to help decide what to look for next.

You must figure out how to capture and control objects, animals, and enemies in order to collect Power Moons so you can power up the Odyssey airship to explore new kingdoms. To progress through the game you must basically uncover and collect a whole lot of hidden collectibles.

There are 24 different creatures to capture, and each new one is listed like a collectable in the “Capture Actions” section of the menu, but Mario can capture other things too, from zips to manhole covers. This capturing mechanic is often required to navigate a particular part of a level or defeat a particular enemy. Most worlds through which you travel are undergoing some sort of major catastrophe that, once resolved, aka, when you finish that side-story, will reward you with multiple Power Moons.

Everything happens, or does not happen, at the player's own, personal pace, in his or her own way of playing, which can change according to the place that the player is in (the player's mood, energy, emotions and thoughts.) Be curious!

So you must learn how to capture things, good things and bad things.

You can explore lots of new kingdoms, each with things that are valuable and special – perhaps just when in that kingdom.

Mario uses a ship named the "Odyssey", a hat-shaped flying vehicle to fly to the game's many kingdoms. He retains many of his moves from the 3D games, such as the Long Jump, Roll, Ground Pound, Ground Pound Jump, Double Jump, Triple Jump, and the returning Dive. Mario and Cappy explore the various kingdoms to collect Power Moons to fuel the Odyssey and battle the Broodals — a team of anthropomorphic rabbit wedding planners hired by Bowser — who steal items including a dress, a cake, and a bouquet from each kingdom to set up Bowser's wedding.

Though not necessary, using Dual Joy-Con (a pair of Joy-Cons as a set) attached to a grip, may allow you to try new things, including new combinations of buttons and ways to do maneuvers, using two thumbsticks!

Mario additionally has some new techniques, including one where he can throw his hat and use it as a platform. The hat can also be used to take control of enemies, which plays a very important role in the game.

Unlike the previous open-world Mario games, Mario only has three sections of health. The game uses a health system similar to the Super Mario Galaxy games, although Mario has unlimited lives; the only penalty for dying is paying up to ten coins. The player can also collect items known as 'Life-Up Hearts' which grant three extra hit points.

Mario also doesn't have any lives in Odyssey. Instead, he will lose 10 Coins upon dying. Cappy can be controlled by a second player in co-op mode.

The Capture mechanic is a new mechanic introduced in Super Mario Odyssey. By throwing his hat at certain enemies with Y Button, Mario can take control of them. This mechanic is used throughout the game and is a fundamental feature part of it, replacing the traditional power-up system in prior games.

For example, Mario can capture a Bullet Bill to fly across large gaps, a Tyrannosaurus to trample things, a bolt of electricity called a Spark Pylon to climb up electric wires, and a tank called a Sherm to fire at enemies and break blocks for passage. Some actions can be accelerated by using motion controls in the Joy-Con controllers, but the game is otherwise fully playable with the Joy-Con attached to the console. Throughout the game, Mario can pick up coins, which come in two types; regular coins and purple ones unique to each kingdom, to spend on items such as new hats and outfits, some of which are required for completing certain objectives.

Odyssey is the first Mario platformer not to feature any lives nor 1-Up Mushrooms nor Game Overs. It is also the first Mario platformer to not feature any type of mushroom.

Each Kingdom has Mario searching for and clearing various objectives in order to obtain items known as Power Moons (the power source of the Odyssey and needed to access the various Kingdoms). Checkpoint flags littered throughout each Kingdom allow Mario to instantly warp to them once activated. Certain levels feature areas called "flat" zones, where Mario is placed in a 2D side-scrolling environment similar to his appearance in the original Super Mario Bros

Basically, in each Kingdom, you must discover the story, then follow it and finish or complete it. What did Browser wreck or ruin? How can you fix what Browser did?

What is cross-over?

But, some things from the Super Mario and or the Kart games just may cross over into the Odyssey game. For instance, Super Maro has a Bonus Dungeon: Superstar Road is unlocked after beating the game, houses some of the hardest levels in the game, and requires collecting each star coin in each world to unlock every level. Brutal Bonus Level: The secret levels in each world are usually harder than the rest of the world’s levels. Every single level in Superstar Road is this as well.

OK, let's review some of what you may have already learned in Super Maro. (Sssh! Quietly now, but some of the things that follow may or may not exist in the latest version of Super Mario for the Switch console, and may or may not work in the earlier version of Super Mario for the Wii U type of console. Discover which things are in your Switch console version of the Mario game, on your own by exploring! Some things may have crossed over just to Odyssey, or just to Super Mario, or not. Try to find out!)

Bubble Gun: The blue Baby Yoshis act like this when shook. Enemies caught in the bubbles turn into coins or power-ups.

The Bus Came Back:

After his absence from the previous game, Bowser Jr. is wreaking havoc alongside the Koopalings once again. Kamek also makes a comeback, working his magic to support the Tower bosses before eventually taking you on himself.

In terms of Bowser Minions, the Big Koopa Troopas, Thwimps, Bony Beetles, Torpedo Teds, their launchers, and Sumo Bros, and even obscure wonders like the Big Amp and Frost/Ice Piranha Plants reappear, the latter returning from Super Paper Mario.

Cartoon Bomb: Lemmy now tosses these, which are styled after his bouncing balls. Ceiling Cling: Iggy doesn't just do this, he flat out walks on the ceiling (not unlike Morton and Roy).

Challenge Run: Challenge Mode has challenges in 4 categories: Time Attack, Coin Collection, 1-Up Rally, and Special. Time Attack challenges have you race against the clock to get to the flagpole, Coin Collection challenges are either about collecting all or most of the coins in a stage, or making it through a stage without collecting too many coins. 1-Up Rally challenges feature bouncing on enemies repeatedly to get 1-Up bonuses, and Special challenges can range from dodging the attacks of 2 Fire Bros. on a single block surrounded by spikes, to making it through Pendulum Castle on Donut Blocks without dashing.

Color-Coded for Your Convenience: Miis have their overalls correspond with what player they are. Player 1 wears Mario's colors, Player 2 wears Luigi's colors, Players 3 and 4 wear Wario's and Waluigi's colors, though they aren't entirely accurate, rather having shades of Mario's color scheme from Mario Bros.

Averted with adult Yoshi. Every one of them is green, regardless of player characters. The baby Yoshis are color-coded according to their different powers.

Composite Character: Besides being a fusion of Toadette and Peach design wise, Peachette is a combination of Peach and Daisy move set wise as she uses both the former’s float ability and the latter’s double jump ability from Super Mario Run.

Continuity Nod:

Slanted pipes, slanted rocks, Munchers, Torpedo Teds, Monty Moles, Baby Yoshis, the style of the overworld, Sumo Bros., Spin Jumping, Flying Squirrel Mario's moves...

This isn't the first time Bowser has taken over Peach's Castle and kept her hostage inside there at the highest point. This is also not the first time that the castle has been taken over by a villain and remade in the villain's own image.

So, how about that dark magic Bowser's been said to have that some of the fanbase (and spinoff game titles) like to pretend doesn't exist? In Mario's first adventure, Bowser was said to use it to transform the land. Here, we finally see him using it progressively to transform Peach's castle into something he prefers. Well, now we know where he gets all the fire and lava!

There's also the Magenta Baby Yoshi's abilities, and the Yellow Baby Yoshi's abilities.

Mini Mario can run up walls. This game is also the first since Super Mario Bros. 3 to have Boom-Boom and the Koopalings in the same game. Boom-Boom and the Koopalings are even the Fortress boss and the Castle bosses, respectively. Unlike in his previous appearance, Boom-Boom fights exactly how he did in his debut. His shell even has spikes again, and he also sprouts wings in his last fight. And like before, the Koopalings are fought in airships instead of the castles.

Like Super Mario World, many of the worlds follow Edible Theme Naming.

The story intro involves the new power-ups flying through the air. And said power-ups come from a giant tree.

Kamek's in, and powers up some bosses. He even supersizes a few enemies as well.

The switch at the other side of the bridge with Bowser does not set off said bridge's self-destruct mechanism on its own accord, but instead sets it off through use of an axe.

The level "Boarding the Airship" in Meringue Clouds has a mechanical Bowser hand (The same one that threw the Mario Bros and the two Toads out from Peach's castle) that acts an obstacle for the first part of the level. For the first few parts of it, the hand acts like the giant pillars from Super Mario World (As seen in Iggy's Castle, Forest Fortress, and Bowser's Castle) and later, it destroys the ground in a fist-shape manner exactly like the Incoming Chomps from Yoshi's Island.

Like in Super Mario World, one of the castles has a secret backdoor.

Follow that Shell!, the real final level, contains only things found in the first Super Mario Bros., as well as a P-Switch and Star Coins. Also, the entire Superstar Road looks like Star Road from Super Mario World, and Follow that Shell! is in the middle, much like Special World.

Freezing-Rain Tower's 2nd half is lifted directly from Castle Crush, which also made an appearance in Brutal Mario.

Just like in many previous Mario games, every Ghost House is guaranteed to have a secret exit.

Soda Jungle 4 and 5, where you are required to find the secret exit to open the path forward, and the regular exit will just loop back to the same level. These levels are found inside of a forest.

One underwater level has currents over bottomless pits that will suck you in and cost you a life if you get pulled under. Super Mario Bros. had this for its underwater levels as well, though without any visual cues.

For the fourth time, one of Bowser Jr's machines is destroyed by breaking the glass dome on top. Of the four fights, it's the third time bullet enemies are used to do so.

Peach's Castle looks exactly like the one from Brutal Mario. The Koopaling order is even the same as in that game, with Iggy and Larry's order switching depending on how the player completes the worlds.

Kamek is initially reluctant to supersize Bowser in the endgame again, presumably because the last time he did that, Bowser knocked him out of the sky. Bowser Jr. keeps him safe this time.

Co-Op Multiplayer: It works exactly the same as its predecessor. Online is still a no-go.

Crown of Power: In Deluxe, Toadette has access to an exclusive Power-Up called the Super Crown, which transforms her into a Princess Peach lookalike named "Peachette" with a Double Jump, Floaty Jump, and Bottomless Pit Rescue Service.

Cumulonemesis: The Foos, which return from New Super Mario Bros. Wii. Just as before, they blow white mist which cover the screen, blinding the player. They only appear in the Meringue Clouds level "Snaking above Mist Valley".
